॥ श्रीमत्जगद्गुरु पंचाचार्याः प्रसीदंतु ।। 
-: प्रस्तावना :- 
परमेश्वराच्या मुखांपासून उत्पन्न झालेल्या कामिकादि वातुलांत 
२८ शिवागमांच्या अंत्यभागांमध्यें वीरशैवमतधर्म अति उत्तम रीतीनें 
स्पष्ट करून सांगण्यांत आलेला आहे. 'चक्रनेमि क्रमेण' या म्हणीप्रमाणें वीरशैव मताला ग्लानि प्राप्त होऊन कालवैपरित्यानें धर्मरूपी धनभांडार अशा शिवागमादिकांचा लोपझाल्यामुळं व स्वधर्मतेजोराशीच्या अभावामुळें मताविषयीं सर्वत्र ग्लानिरूपी अंधकार पसरला आहे. चालू काळांत 'स्वधर्माचलितान् राजा विनीय स्थापयेत्पथि' या कार्योक्तीप्रमाणें दुःस्थितीत असलेल्या आपल्या प्रजेला सन्मार्गावर आणण्यास सध्याचे राज्यकर्ते आमच्या धर्माचे नसले तरी (परधर्मी असलेतरी) आपापल्या धर्माचें पुनरुज्जीवन करणाऱ्यांना मात्र ते प्रतिबंधक न होतां अनुकूलच झालेले आहेत. हे समाजाचे सुदैवच होय. 
   अशा सुसंधीत यथाशक्ति धर्मोन्नति करणें हैं प्रत्येक धर्माभिमान्याचे कर्तव्य आहे. 
   धर्मजागृति करण्याचे अनेक उपाय आहेत. त्यांपैकी सर्वांना विकत घेण्यास सुलभ, दुसऱ्याच्या मदतीखेरीज स्वतांलाच समजण्यास सुगम, आणि समजून त्याप्रमाणें वागण्यास योग्य असे करण्यास पुरातन असे दुर्मिळ मतग्रंथांचे मुद्रण करून त्यांचा प्रचार करणे हा एक उपाय आहे. हा उपाय आम्ही यथाशक्ति हाती घेतला आहे. तो पूर्ण करणे हे जगन्नियंत्या परमेश्वराकडे आहे. 
  वीरशैव धर्मग्रंथ कानडी, तेलगू, अरबी लिपिंत व संस्कृत भाषेत अधिक असल्याचे दिसून येते. त्या ग्रंथांपैकी प्राकृत टीका असलेले ग्रंथ फारच अल्प प्रमाणांत आहेत. व तेही कानडी, तेलुगू, अरबी या भाषामध्येंच आहेत. या योगानें महाराष्ट्रिय वीरशैव बांधवांना धर्मग्रंथांचा ज्ञानोदय होऊन धर्मजागृती होणार नाही. ती व्हावयास पाहिजे असल्यास मराठी टीकेनेंच होणार असें जाणून धर्मग्रंथ मराठी टीकेसह छापण्याचे कार्य सुरू केले आहे. प्रथम याच सद्धेतूनें श्रीमंत कै. वा. धर्मोद्धारक रा. व. अप्पासाहेब वारद यांनी वीरशैव लिंगीब्राह्मण धर्मग्रंथमालेचा आरंभ करून अनेक मत ग्रंथाचे मराठी टीकेसह मुद्रण करून वीरशैव समाजावर महदुपकार केले आहेत. त्या मालेपैकीं पांचवा ग्रंथ सुप्रबोधागमांतर्गत “पंचाचार्य पंचमोत्पत्ति प्रकरण " हा आहे. सध्या हा ग्रंथ ग्राहकांना दुर्मिळ झाल्यामुळें या आम्ही आरंभलेल्या श्री बालतपस्वी कृपापोषित धर्मवीर ग्रंथ रत्न मालेंत 'सुप्रबोधागम' या नावानें (दुसरें नांव न ठेवतां पूर्वीच्याच नावानें) छापिला आहे. हें ३ रें ग्रंथरत्न होय. यामध्यें वीरशैव  मतस्थापक, वीरशैव जगद्गुरु अशा पंचाचार्यांचा अवतार म्हणजे पंचमुखी परमेश्वराच्या सद्योजात मुखापासून रेवणाराध्य, वामदेव मुखापासून मरुळाराध्य, अघोर मुखापासून एकोरामाराध्य, तत्पुरुष मुखापासून पंडिताराध्य व ईशान मुखापासून विश्वाराध्य उद्धवलेले विषय; गोत्र, सूत्र, उपसूत्रें विवाह निषेध व महाचार्य, उपाचार्य यांच्या वागणुकीचा विषय सांगितलेला आहे. आणि परमेश्वराच्या ऊर्ध्वमुखापासून उत्पन्न झालेल्या पंचवक्त्रगणाधीश्वराच्या पांच मुखांपासून अनुक्रमें मखारि, कालारि, पुरारि, स्मरारि, वेदारि हे पंचम; आणि यांच्या पासून उत्पन्न झालेले उपपंचम यांचे वर्णन आहे. सूत्रगोत्र वगैरे वाचकांना 
समजण्यास सोपे जावे या उद्देशानें त्यांचे कोष्टक शेवटी दिलेले आहे. 
प्रकाशक.
data.english:
Preface

The Veerashaiva religion has been very well explained in the concluding portions of the twenty-eight Śiva Āgamas such as the Kāmika Āgama up to Vātula, which are said to have originated from the mouths of Parameśvara. According to the saying “like the rim of a wheel in sequence,” due to the decline of the Veerashaiva doctrine over time, and because the treasure-house of dharma in the form of Śiva Āgamas and similar texts has disappeared, and due to the absence of the radiance of one’s own dharma, the darkness in the form of decline has spread everywhere regarding the doctrine. In the present time, according to the statement of duty “the king should discipline and establish on the right path those who have deviated from their own dharma,” although the current rulers are not of our religion (even if they belong to another religion), they have not become obstacles but rather supportive to those who revive their respective dharma. This is indeed the good fortune of society.

In such an opportunity, it is the duty of every follower of dharma to promote the upliftment of dharma to the best of their ability.

There are many ways to awaken dharma. Among them, one method is to print and propagate rare ancient doctrinal texts in such a way that they are affordable to all, easy to understand without the help of others, and suitable to follow after understanding them. This method we have undertaken to the best of our ability. Its completion rests with the Supreme Lord, the controller of the universe.

It is observed that Veerashaiva religious texts are mostly found in Kannada, Telugu, Arabic scripts, and in the Sanskrit language. Among these, texts with Prakrit and commentaries are very few, and even those are only in Kannada, Telugu, and Arabic languages. Due to this, Maharashtrian Veerashaiva brethren cannot attain knowledge of these religious texts, and thus there will be no awakening of dharma. Realizing that such awakening can occur only through Marathi commentary, the work of publishing religious texts with Marathi explanations has been undertaken. First, with this very intention, the wealthy late Appasaheb Varad began the Veerashaiva Lingi-Brahmin religious text series and rendered great service to the Veerashaiva community by printing many doctrinal texts with Marathi commentary. Among that series, the fifth text is the “Panchacharya Panchamotpatti Prakarana” contained in the Suprabodha Āgama. At present, as this text has become rare for readers, we have printed it under the same name “Suprabodha Āgama” (without giving it a new name) in the ‘Shri Balatapasvi Kripaposhit Dharmaveer Granth Ratna Mala’ series initiated by us. This is the third jewel in the series.

In this, the subjects described include the manifestation of the five Āchāryas—founders of the Veerashaiva doctrine and Jagadgurus—namely: Revanaaradhya from the Sadyojata face of the five-faced Parameśvara, Marularadhya from the Vamadeva face, Ekoramaradhya from the Aghora face, Panditaradhya from the Tatpurusha face, and Vishwaradhya from the Ishana face; as well as topics such as gotra, sutra, sub-sutras, prohibitions in marriage, and the conduct of Mahacharyas and Upacharyas. Further, from the upward face of Parameśvara arose the Panchavaktra Ganadhishwara, and from his five faces respectively emerged Makhari, Kalari, Purari, Smarari, and Vedari—the five Panchamas—and from them originated the sub-Panchamas; their descriptions are also given. For the ease of understanding of readers regarding sutra, gotra, etc., their charts are provided at the end.

Publisher

ईश्वरपंचमुखानि ।
सद्योजातश्च प्रथमो वामदेवो द्वितीयकः ॥ 
अघोरश्व तृतीयस्तु तत्पुरुषश्वतुर्थकः ॥ १ ॥ 
ईशानः पंचमश्चेति मुखानि मम सर्वशः ॥ 
तान्याननानि गोत्राणि वेदोक्तानि न संशयः ॥ २ ॥
पाशुपततंत्रे.

सद्योजातो भवेद्भूमिर्वामदेवस्तथा जलम् ॥ अघोरश्चाग्निरित्युक्तस्तत्पुरुषो वायुरुच्यते ॥ 
ईशानो गगनाकारः पंच ब्रह्ममयं जगत् ॥ १ ॥
सुप्रबोधागमे.

पंचगोत्राधिकारिणः ।
नंदी श्रृंगी तथा वीरो वृषभः स्कंद एव च ॥ 
मत्स्वरूपाः समुत्पन्नाः पंच गोत्राधिकारिणः ॥ १ ॥
पाशुपततंत्रे.

पंचगोत्रसमुत्पन्नाः ।
दारुकः शंकुकर्णश्च रेणुको धेनुकर्णकः ॥ 
विश्वकर्णश्च पंचैते पंचगोत्रसमुद्भवाः ॥ १ ॥ 
पाशुपततंत्रे.

कृतयुगे तन्नामानि ।
एतेषां प्रतिनामानि युगभेदेन सर्वशः ॥ 
एकाक्षरो द्वक्षरश्च त्र्यक्षरश्चतुरक्षरः ॥ 
पंचाक्षरः कृतयुगे पंच नामानि सर्वशः ॥ १ ॥
पाशुपततंत्रे.

त्रेतायुगे तन्नामानि ।
एकवक्त्रो द्विवक्त्रश्च त्रिवक्त्रश्चतुराननः ॥
पंचवक्त्रश्च त्रेतायां पंच नामानि सर्वशः ॥ १ ॥
पाशुपतंतंत्रे.

द्वापारे तन्नामानि ।
द्वापारे दारुकश्चेति शंकुकर्णों दितीयकः ॥ 
रेणुकस्तु तृतीयः स्याद्धेनुकर्णश्चतुर्थकः ॥ 
विश्वकर्णश्च पंचैते पंच नामानि सर्वशः ॥ १ ॥
पाशुपततंत्रे.

कलौ तन्नामानि ।.
मरुळश्चैकरामश्च रेणुकः पंडितस्तथा ॥ 
विश्वाराध्य इति प्रोक्ताः कलौ पंचार्यनायकाः ॥ १ ॥
पाशुपततंत्रे.
data.english:
Īśvara tells Pārvatī: “O Pārvatī, my first face is Sadyojāta, the second is Vāmadeva, the third is Aghora, the fourth is Tatpuruṣa, and the fifth is Īśāna. These five faces and these gotras are all declared in the Vedas; there is no doubt in this.”



The Sadyojāta face is earth, the Vāmadeva face is water, the Aghora face is fire, the Tatpuruṣa face is air, and the Īśāna face is space; in this way, this world is of the nature of the five Brahmas, that is, composed of the five elements and entirely of the form of Śiva.


Nandī, Bhṛṅgī, and similarly Vīra, Vṛṣabha, and Skanda—these five, being of my own form, the five authorities of the five gotras, were born from the five faces.


Dāruka, Śaṅkukarna, Reṇuka, Dhenukarna, and Viśvakarna—these five were born from those five gotras.



According to the progression of the yugas, all of these (the authorities of the five gotras) have had different names. In Kṛtayuga, their five names were Ekākṣara, Dvyakṣara, Tryakṣara, Caturakṣara, and Pañcākṣara.



In Tretāyuga, their five names were Ekavaktra, Dvivaktra, Trivaktra, Caturānana, and Pañcavaktra.


In Dvāparayuga, the five names of those authorities of the five gotras became Dāruka, Śaṅkukarna, Reṇuka, Dhenukarna, and Viśvakarna.


In Kaliyuga, the five names of those authorities of the five gotras became Maruḷa, Ekorāma, Reṇuka, Paṇḍita, and Viśvārādhya.

सुप्रबोधागमे पंचाचार्योत्पत्तिः ॥
पार्वत्युवाच ।
भगवन्ये त्वया प्रोक्ताः पंच पीठाधिदेवताः । 
स्वतंत्रा मुख्यगुरवो महांतश्चेति विश्रुताः ॥१॥ 
तथैवमस्वतंत्राणां प्रभेदं वक्तुमर्हसि । 
इत्येवं गिरिजापृष्टो भगवान्भूतभावनः ।। 
अस्वतंत्रगुरूणां च प्रभेदं वक्तुमारभत् ।।२।।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
पूर्व मम मुखाञ्जातः सद्योजाताच्च रेणुकः । 
लीलया चासृजत्सूत्रं पड़वीडीनामकं महत् ॥३॥
स एव रेवणाराध्यो भूत्वा लीलामथाकरोत् । 
तल्लीलया समुत्पन्नान्युपसूत्राणि द्वादश ॥४॥
 पुराणं पच्छकंथा च षडंग: सुरगिस्तथा । 
महिषी दिगंबरश्चैव वेणी भित्तिस्तथैव च ।।५।। 
मोरट: चैव नाटश्च शौरी मुसडिकस्तथा । 
महासूत्रेण संयुक्ता उपसूत्रास्त्रयोदश ।। ६ ।।
एते सर्वेऽप्यस्वतंत्रा जाता अपि महात्मना ।
पार्वत्युवाच ।
महाचार्येण संभूताः कथं तेप्यस्वतंत्रकाः ॥७॥ 
अस्वातंत्र्ये कारणं किमेतद्विस्तरतो वद ।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
सद्योजातमुखोत्पत्तिराहित्येन तथैव च ।।८।। 
तदास्यकलशस्यापि हरिद्वर्णमयस्य च । अधिकारित्वराहित्यादनीशास्योद्भवत्वतः च ।।९।। प्रसादपंचवर्णाख्यमंत्रस्यास्य महामते । 
उपदेष्टत्वराहित्यात्कंजपत्रायतेक्षणे । वीरगोत्राभिधानात्तदृगाद्यागमजातिषु ॥१०॥ अधिकारित्वराहित्याद्वीरशैवालयेषु च । 
दीक्षालिंगोपदेशादिष्वकर्तारस्ततोऽभवन् ॥११॥
पार्वत्युवाच ।
कथं कुर्वत्यस्वतंत्रा वीरशैवालयेषु च । 
दीक्षोपदेशनं चैव लिंगधारणपूर्वकम् ॥१२॥ 
एतद्विस्तार्य भगवन्वक्तुमर्हसि सांप्रतम् ।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
द्वादशाप्युपसूत्रज्ञा अस्वतंत्रा अपि स्वयम् ॥१३॥ 
महासूत्राधिपतिना चोपदेशादनंतरम् । 
तद‌नुग्राहतस्तेषां गोत्रप्रवरवर्णकैः ।॥१४॥ 
कलशैर्मंत्रदंडाद्यैः कमंडलुसमन्वितै: । 
वीरशैवालयेष्वेते चास्वतंत्राः प्रवर्तकाः ॥ १५॥
पार्वत्युवाच ।
त्रयोदशोपसूत्राणामुपदेशोऽभत्रत्वथम् । 
गुरुः कोऽभूत्साक्षिणः के मंत्रः कः कलशश्च कः ॥१६॥ 
किं बीजं किंविधं लिंगं कस्यां दिशि समाचरेत् । 
इतीशान्या च संपृष्टो भगवानब्रवीद्वचः ॥१७॥
ईश्वर उवाच ।
रेवणार्यसमुद्भूतास्त्रयोदशविधाश्च ये । 
उपस्सूत्रज्ञकास्तेषामुपदेशः प्रवक्ष्यते ॥१८॥ 
रेवणार्य हरिद्वर्ण सद्योजातात्मकं मुखम् । 
कलशं मध्यमं बीजं नकारं विलिखेत्ततः ॥१९॥ 
नकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं विन्यसेदुधः । 
अधिदेवं रेवणार्य मध्ये संभावयेद्गुरुम् २०। 
तत्स्थाने प्राक्तने रक्तं वामदेवमुखात्मकम् । 
कलशं च मकाराख्यबीजे संस्थापयेद्बुधः ॥२१॥ 
तत्राधिदैवतं चैत्र मरुळाराध्यनामकम् । 
साक्षीभूतं गुरुश्रेष्ठं । कारयित्वा ततः परम् ॥ २२ ॥ 
तत्स्थाने दक्षिणे कृष्णवर्णाघोरमुखात्मकम् । 
कलशं च शिकाराख्यं महाबीजं लिखेत्ततः ॥२३॥ 
शिकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं स्थापयेद्बुधः  । 
तत्राधिदैवतं चैकोरामाराध्यं तथैव च । २४।। 
साक्षीभूताधिदेवं तं कारयित्वा ततः परम् । 
तत्स्थाने पश्चिमे शुभ्रवर्ण तत्पुरुषात्मकम् ।२५। 
कलशं च वकाराख्यं महाबीजं लिखेत्ततः ।
वकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं स्थापयेद्बुधः ॥२६॥ 
तत्राधिदैवतं चैत्र पंडिताराध्यनामकम् । 
साक्षीभूतं कारयित्वा तथैत्र च ततः परम् ॥२७॥
तत्स्थाने चोत्तरे पीतवर्णेशानमुखात्मकम् । 
कलशं तद्यकाराख्यं महाबीजं लिखेत्ततः ॥२८॥ 
यकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं स्थापयेद्बुधः । 
तत्र विश्वाराध्यदेवं साक्षीकृत्याधिदैवतम् ॥२९॥ 
ततः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि रेवणाराध्यलीलया । 
समुद्भूतोपसुत्रज्ञास्रूयोदशविधाश्च ये ॥३०॥ 
आगमोक्तविधानेन ॐ ऱ्हां ऱ्हीं ऱ्हूं ऱ्हैं ऱ्हौं परम् । 
नमः शिवायेति मंत्रं दशाक्षरमन्नुनुत्तमम् । ३१॥ 
प्रसादाख्यं महामंत्रमुपदिष्टाः पृथक् पृथक् । 
रेवणाराध्यगुरुणा हरिद्वर्णमयं तथा । ३२॥ 
लिंगं धृतास्ततः सर्वे तन्मतालंबिनश्च ते । 
तस्मात्तत्पड़विडी चैव पुराणं पच्छकंथकम् ॥३३॥ 
षडंगः सुरगः चैत्र महिषी च दिगंबरम् । 
वेणी भित्तिश्च मोरटं नाटिः शौरी तथैव च ॥३४॥ 
मुसडीति महासूत्रसंयुक्तास्ते त्रयोदश । 
एवं भेदवतां सद्योजाताननसमुद्भव: ।॥३५॥ 
वीरगोत्राधिनाथश्च सिंहासनपतिश्च यः । 
रेवणाराध्यसन्नामा जगद्गुरुतमश्च सः ॥३६॥ एभिस्त्रयोदशविधैरुपदिष्टाश्च सर्वशः । 
तेषां चैत्र गुरूणां च लिंगधारणकर्मणि ॥३७॥ 
दीक्षोपदेशयोश्चैव विवाहादौ तथैत्र च । 
चरस्थापनपट्टाभिषेकेषु शुभकर्मसु ॥३८॥ 
तथैवानुग्रहे चैव शिक्षणेऽपि तथैव च । 
आह्वाने च विसर्जे च सद्योजातमुखोद्भवः ॥ ३९॥ 
परमो रेवणाराध्यो मुख्यकर्ता गुरूत्तमः । 
तस्मान्मन्मुखसंजाताः स्वतंत्राश्चेति विश्रुताः ॥४०॥ 
तेभ्यो ये च समुत्पन्ना उपसुत्रास्त्रयोदश । 
अमुख्यास्तेप्यस्वतंत्रा महाचार्यानुगाश्च ते ॥४१॥ 
तेभ्यश्चैवोपदिष्टास्तु सामान्या वीरशैवकाः । 
ते पंचमा इति ख्याता उपपूर्वास्तथेतरे ॥४२॥

इति रेवणाचार्यदीक्षाप्रकरणम्

[1] Pārvatī says, “O Bhagavan, the five pīṭhādhipatis that you have described are said by you to be completely independent and prominent gurus;

[2] then, in the same way, please kindly tell me the distinctions of those who are not independent.” After Pārvatī asked in this manner, the Supreme Lord, the creator of all beings,

[3] began to explain the distinctions of the dependent (non-independent) gurus. Īśvara says, “First, from my Sadyojāta face, Reṇuka was born, and by his natural divine play he produced a great sūtra called Paḍviḍī.

[4] He later became Revaṇārādhya and engaged in divine play, and through that play twelve subsidiary sūtras (upasūtras) were produced.

[5–6] Purāṇa, Pacchakanthā, Ṣaḍaṅga, Suragi, Māhaṣī, Digambara, Veṇī, Bhitti, Morata, Nāṭa, Śaurī, and Musaḍika—these are the twelve upasūtras, and together with the Paḍviḍī Mahāsūtra they become thirteen in total.

[7] Although all of these have originated from the great being ( Renuka ), they should still be understood as dependent.” Pārvatī asks, “Though they have originated from the Mahāchārya, how are they not independent?

[8] And what is the reason for their being dependent? Please explain all this to me in detail.” Īśvara says, “They are not directly born from the Sadyojāta face, and moreover,

[9] they do not possess authority over the green-colored kalasha belonging to that (Sadyojāta) face. Since they are not born directly from the mouth of Parameśvara,

[10-11] they are not entitled to impart the Prasāda Pañcākṣarī mantra; likewise, though they declare the name of the Vīra gotra but they do not have authority over the Ṛgveda and Āgamas , nor over any religious functions in the houses of Vīraśaivas. Therefore, they are not entitled to perform dīkṣā or liṅgopadeśa."

[12] Pārvatī asks, “If they are not independent, then how do they perform initiation with liṅga-wearing and give instruction in the houses of Vīraśaivas?

[13] O Bhagavan, explain this to me in detail now.” Īśvara says, “Although the knowers of the twelve upasūtras are not themselves independent,

[14–15] after receiving instruction from the lord of the Mahāsūtra ( Renuka ), by his grace they carry out religious rites such as initiation and instruction in the houses of Vīraśaivas along with gotra, pravara, varṇa, kalasha, mantra, staff, and water-pot.

[16] Pārvatī asks, “How is instruction given to these thirteen upasūtras? Who is their guru? Who are the witnesses? What is their mantra? What kalasha,

[17] seed (bīja), and liṅga do they have? And what are their directions?” After Pārvatī asked in this manner, Bhagavan began to tell her.

[18] Īśvara says, “I shall explain the method of instruction for the thirteen upasūtra-knowers who originated from Revaṇācārya.

[19–20] Revaṇārādhya has a green color, the Sadyojāta face, and the middle kalasha; his bīja-mantra is the syllable ‘na’. Then, in the place of the great bīja-mantra ‘na’, the kalasha should be established, and the presiding deity, Guru Revaṇārya, should be invoked.

[21–22] To his east, with red color and the Vāmadeva face, the kalasha should be established at the place of the bīja-mantra ‘ma’; the presiding deity there, Maruḷārādhya, should be made the witness.

[23–24] Then to his south, with black color and the Aghora face, the kalasha should be established at the place of the great bīja-mantra ‘śi’; the presiding deity there, Ekorāmārādhya, should also be made a witnessing deity.

[25–27] In the west, there should be a white-colored kalasha of the Tatpuruṣa aspect, and the bīja-mantra ‘va’ should be written; then the kalasha should be established there, and the presiding deity Paṇḍitārādhya should be made the witness.

[28–29] Similarly, in the north, taking a yellow-colored kalasha of the Īśāna aspect, the bīja-mantra ‘ya’ should be written; then the kalasha should be established there, and Viśvārādhya, the presiding deity there, should be made the witness.

[30] Thereafter, I will tell you about the thirteen upasūtra-knowers that arose from the divine play of Revaṇārādhya.

[31] According to the Āgamic injunction, the ten-syllabled mantra “Om r̥hāṁ r̥hīṁ r̥hūṁ r̥haiṁ r̥hauṁ namaḥ śivāya” is considered the best among all.

[32–33] This great mantra called Prasāda must be imparted separately. Just as Guru Revaṇārādhya has worn a green-colored liṅga, so also his followers wear a green-colored liṅga.

[33–35] Thus Paḍviḍī, Purāṇa, Pacchakantā, Ṣaḍaṅga, Suragi, Māhaṣī, Digambara, Veṇī, Bhitti, Māreṭa, Nāṭi, Śaurī, and likewise Musaḍī—together with the Mahāsūtra—become thirteen. These thirteen distinctions described are all said to have originated from the Sadyojāta face.

[36] The primal lord and throne-holder of the Vīra gotra, Revaṇārādhya, is the supreme Jagadguru.

[37–38] From these thirteen, instruction of all kinds is given. However, among all these gurus, at the time of liṅga-dhāraṇa, when initiation or instruction is to be given, at the time of marriage, at the time of consecrating ( pattabhiseka ) or installing pontiffs, during auspicious rituals,

[39–40] and similarly when granting grace or punishment, and at the time of invocation and dismissal, the one born from the Sadyojāta face—the greatest Revaṇārādhya Guru alone—is the principal performer. Therefore, only those born directly from my faces are called independent (they alone are independent).

[41–42] Those thirteen upasūtra-knowers who have originated from them are not principal or independent in any function, but merely followers of the Mahāchārya. Those Vīraśaivas who receive initiation from them are considered ordinary. These are called Pañcamas, and those who arise from them are called Upapañcamas.

Here ends the section on the initiation of Revaṇācārya's Pitha.

पार्वत्युवाच ।
भगवन्ये त्वया प्रोक्ताः पंचपीठाधिदेवताः । 
स्वतंत्रा मुख्यगुरवो महांतश्चेति विश्रुताः ॥४३॥ 
तथैवमस्वतंत्राणां प्रभेदं वक्तुमर्हसि । 
इत्येवं गिरिजापृष्टो भगवान्भूतभावनः ॥४४॥ 
अस्वतंत्रगुरूणां च प्रभेदं वक्तुमारभत् ।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
पूर्व मम मुखाञ्जतो वामदेवाच्च दारुकः ॥४५॥ 
लीलया व्यसृजत्सूत्रं वृष्टिनाम महत्तरम् । 
स एव मरुळाराध्यो भुत्वा लीलामथाकरोत् ॥ ४६ ॥ 
तल्लीलया समुत्पन्नान्युपसुत्राणि द्वादश । 
लोहकंथा स्वर्णकंथा श्रृंगी मसणिरेव च ॥४७॥ 
कुठारश्च तथा मैत्री कठारश्चामरी तथा । 
कवाटंः कुक्षकंथा च ज्वलत्कंथा तथैव च ॥४८॥ 
सिंही चैते महावृष्टिसूत्रयुक्तास्त्रयोदश । 
एते सर्वेऽप्य स्वतंत्रा जाता अपि महात्मना ॥४९॥
पार्वत्युवाच ।
महाचार्येण संभूताः कथं तेऽप्यस्वतंत्रकाः । 
अस्वातंत्र्ये कारण किमेतद्विस्तरतो वद ॥५०॥
ईश्वर उवाच ।
वामदेवमुखोत्पत्तिराहित्येन तथैव च । 
तदास्यकलशस्यापि रक्त वर्णमयस्य च ॥५१॥ अधिकारित्वराहित्यादनीशास्योद्भवत्वतः 
नंदिगोत्राभिधानाच्च मायापंचाक्षरस्य च ॥५२॥ 
उपदेष्टत्वराहित्यादृगाद्यागमजातिषु । अधिकारित्वराहित्याद्वीरशैवालयेषु च ॥५३॥ दीक्षालिंगोपदेशादिष्वकर्तारस्ततोऽभवन् ।
पार्वत्युवाच ।
कथं कुर्वत्यस्वतंत्रा वीरशैवालयेषु च ॥५४॥ 
दीक्षोपदेशनं चैव लिंगधारणपूर्वकम् । 
एतद्विस्तार्य भगवन्वक्तुमर्हसि सांप्रतम् ॥५५॥
ईश्वर उवाच ।
त्रयोदशोपसूत्रज्ञा अस्वतंत्रा अपि स्वयम् । 
महासूत्राधिपतिना चोपदेशादनंतरम् ।।५६।। 
तदनुग्राहतस्तेषां गोत्रप्रवरवर्णकैः ।
कलशैर्मंत्रदंडाद्यैः कमंडलुसमन्वितैः ॥५७॥ 
वीरशैवालयेष्वेते चास्वतंत्राः प्रवर्तकाः।
पार्वत्युवाच ।
त्रयोदशोपसूत्राणामुपदेशोऽभवत्कथम् ॥५८॥ 
गुरुः कोऽभूत्साक्षिणः के मंत्रः कः कलशश्च कः । 
किं बीजं किं विधं लिंगं कस्यां दिशि समाचरेत् ।।५९।। 
इतीशान्या च संप्पृष्टो भगवानब्रवीद्वचः ।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
मरुळाराध्यसंभूतास्त्रयोदशविधाश्च ये ॥६०॥ 
उपसूत्रज्ञकास्तेषामुपदेशः प्रवक्ष्यते । 
मरुळार्यस्य रक्ताभं वामदेवमुखात्मकम् ।।६१॥ 
कलशं मध्यमं बीजं मकारं विलिखेत्ततः । 
मकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं तं न्यसेद्बुधः ॥६२॥ मरुळाराध्यमध्यक्षं मध्ये संभावयेद्गुरुम् । 
तत्स्थाने प्राक्तने कृष्णवर्णाघोरसुखात्मकम् ॥६३॥ 
कलशं च शिकाराख्यं महाबीजं लिखेत्ततः । 
शिकाराख्ये महाबीजे तत्करीरं न्यसेद्बुधः ॥६४॥ 
तत्राधिदैवतं चैकोरामाराध्यं तथैव च 
साक्षीभूताधिदैवं तं कारयित्वा ततः परम् ॥६५॥ 
तत्स्थाने दक्षिणे शुभ्रवर्ण तत्पुरुषात्मकम् । 
कलशं च वकाराख्यं महाबीजं लिखेत्ततः ॥६६॥
वकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं तत्र विन्यसेत् । 
तत्राधिदैवतं चैव पंडिताराध्यनामकम् ॥६७॥
साक्षीभूतं कारयित्वा तथैव च ततः परम् । 
तत्स्थाने पश्चिमे पीतवर्णेशानमुखात्मकम् ॥६८॥ 
कलशं तद्यकाराख्यं महाबीजं लिखेत्ततः । 
यकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं स्थापयेद्बुधः ॥६९॥ 
विश्वाराध्याभिधं चैव कृत्वा वै साक्षिणं पुनः । 
तत्स्थाने चोत्तरे चैव हरिद्वर्णात्मकं तथा ॥७०॥ 
कलशं तं नकाराख्यं महाबीजं लिखेत्ततः । 
नकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं स्थापयेद्बुधः ॥७१॥ 
रेणुकाराध्यमध्यक्षं साक्षिणं तं विधाय च । 
ततः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि मरुळाराध्यलीलया ॥७२॥ 
समुद्भूतोपसूत्रज्ञास्त्रयोदशविधाश्च ते । 
आगमोक्तविधानेन ॐ ऱ्हां ऱ्हीं ऱ्हूं ऱ्हैं चाप्यतः ॥७३॥ 
नमः शिवाय मंत्रांतं नवाक्षरमनुत्तमम् । 
मायापंचाक्षराख्यं ते ह्युपदिष्टाः पृथक् पृथक् ॥७४॥ 
मरुळाराध्यगुरुणा रक्तवर्णमयं तथा । 
लिंगं दध्रुस्तथा सर्वे तन्मतालंबिनश्च ते ॥७५॥

शृंगी च मसणिश्चैव कुठारो मैत्रिकः परम् । 
कठारश्चामरी चैव कवाटं च ततः परम् ॥ 
कुक्षिकंथा ज्वलत्कंथा सिंही चेति महेश्वरि ॥ महासूत्रसमायुक्तास्त्रयोदश समीरिताः । 
एवं भेदवतां वामदेवाननसमुद्भवः ॥७६॥ 
नंदिगोत्राधिनाथश्च सिंहासनपतिश्च यः । 
मरुळाराध्यसन्नामा जगद्गुरुतमश्च सः ॥७७॥ एभिस्त्रयोदशविधैरुपदिष्टाश्च सर्वशः ।

चरस्थापनपट्टाभिषेकेषु शुभकर्मसु ॥७९॥ 
निग्रहेऽनुग्रहे चैवमाह्वाने च विसर्जने ।

[46] By his natural divine play, he produced a great sūtra named Vṛṣṭi. Later, he became Maruḷārādhya and engaged in divine play,

[47–49] and through that play twelve upasūtras were produced: Lohakanthā, Kharṇakanthā, Śṛṅgī, Masaṇī, Kuṭhāra, Maitrī, Kaṭhāra, Cāmarī, Kavāṭa, Kukṣakanthā, Jvalatkanthā, and Siṁhī. These twelve, along with the Vṛṣṭi Mahāsūtra, make a total of thirteen. Although all these have originated from the great being ( Dāruka ), they should be understood as dependent.”

[50] Pārvatī asks, “Though they have originated from the Mahāchārya, how are they not independent? And what is the reason for their dependence? Please explain all this to me in detail.”

[51–54] Īśvara says, “They are not directly born from the Vāmadeva face, and they also do not have authority over the red-colored kalasha of that Vāmadeva face. Since they are not born from the mouth of Parameśvara, they are not entitled to impart the Māyā Pañcākṣarī mantra of the Nandī gotra. Likewise, they have no authority over the Vedas and Āgamas such as the Ṛgveda, nor over any religious functions in the houses of Vīraśaivas. Therefore, they are not entitled to perform dīkṣā or liṅgopadeśa.”

[55] Pārvatī asks, “If they are not independent, then how do they perform initiation with liṅga-wearing and give instruction in the houses of Vīraśaivas? Please explain this to me in detail.”

[56–59] Īśvara says, “Although the knowers of the twelve upasūtras are not themselves independent, after receiving instruction from the lord of the Mahāsūtra ( Dāruka ), by his grace they conduct religious rites such as initiation and instruction in the houses of Vīraśaivas along with gotra, pravara, varṇa, kalasha, mantra, staff, and water-pot.” Pārvatī asks, “How is instruction given to these thirteen upasūtras? Who is their guru? Who are the witnesses? What is their mantra? What kalasha, bīja, and liṅga do they have? And what are their directions?”

[60] After Pārvatī asked in this manner, Bhagavan Parameśvara began to tell her.

[61–62] Īśvara says, “I shall explain the method of instruction for the thirteen upasūtra-knowers who originated from Maruḷārādhya. Maruḷārādhya has the Vāmadeva aspect, a red-colored kalasha, and the bīja-mantra ‘ma’ is to be written in the center. Then the kalasha should be established at the place of this great bīja-mantra. The presiding guru Maruḷārādhya should be invoked in the center.

[63–65] To his east, there should be a black/dark blue-colored kalasha of the Aghora aspect, and the bīja-mantra ‘śi’ should be written; the kalasha should be established there, and the presiding deity Ekorāmārādhya should be made the witness.

[66–68] To his south, there should be a white-colored kalasha of the Tatpuruṣa aspect, and the bīja-mantra ‘va’ should be written; the kalasha should be established there, and the presiding deity Paṇḍitārādhya should also be made the witness. Then, to his west, there should be a yellow-colored kalasha of the Īśāna aspect, and the bīja-mantra ‘ya’ should be written; the kalasha should be established there, and the presiding deity Viśvārādhya should be made the witness.

[70–72] To his north, there should be a green-colored kalasha, and the bīja-mantra ‘na’ should be written; the kalasha should be established there, and the presiding deity Reṇukārādhya should be made the witness.

[72–74] Further, O Pārvatī, I shall describe the divine play of Maruḷārādhya. From his play, thirteen upasūtra-knowers arose, and according to the Āgamic injunction, they are to be instructed separately in the excellent nine-syllabled mantra “Om r̥hāṁ r̥hīṁ r̥hūṁ r̥haiṁ namaḥ śivāya” called Māyā Pañcākṣarī.

[75] Just as Guru Maruḷārādhya has worn a red-colored liṅga, so also his followers wear a red-colored liṅga.

[76] Thus Vṛṣṭi, Lohakanthā, Svarṇakanthā, and similarly Śṛṅgī, Masaṇī, Kuṭhāra, Maitrī, Kaṭhāra, Cāmarī, Kavāṭa, Kukṣikanthā, Jvalatkanthā, and Siṁhī—together with the Mahāsūtra—become thirteen. These thirteen distinctions described are said to have originated from the aspect of Vāmadeva face ( Daruka )

[77] The primal lord and throne-holder of the Nandī gotra, Maruḷārādhya, is the supreme Jagadguru.

[78–80] From these thirteen, all kinds of instruction are given. However, among all these gurus, at the time of liṅga-dhāraṇa, when initiation or instruction is to be given, at the time of marriage, at the installation of caramurtis or consecration of pontiffs, during auspicious rites, and when granting grace or discipline, and at the time of invocation and dismissal, the one born from the Vāmadeva face—the greatest Maruḷārādhya Guru alone—is the principal performer.

[81–82] Therefore, only those born from my faces are called independent; they alone are independent. Those thirteen upasūtra-knowers who have originated from them are not principal or independent in any function, but merely followers of the Mahāchārya. Those Vīraśaivas who receive initiation from them are considered ordinary. These gurus are called Pañcamas, and those who arise from them are called Upapañcamas.

त्वया प्रोक्ताश्च भगवन्पंच पीठाधिदेवताः । 
स्वतंत्रा मुख्यगुरवो महांतश्चेति विश्रुताः ॥८३॥ 
तथैवमस्वतंत्राणां प्रभेदं वक्तुमर्हसि । 
इत्येवं गिरिजापृष्टो भगवान् भूतभावनः ॥८४॥ 
अस्वतंत्रगुरूणां च प्रभेदं वक्तुमारभत् ।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
पूर्व मद्वदनाञ्जातश्चाघोराच्छंकुकर्णकः ॥८५॥ 
लीलयैवासृजत्सूत्रंमुक्तागुच्छं महत्तरम् । 
(it should be Lambana sutram instead of muktaguccha)
स एकोरामनामासीत् स च लीलामथाकरोत् ॥ ८६ ॥ 
तल्लीलया समुत्पन्नान्युपसूत्राणि द्वादश ।
 गोणीकंथा च दंती च जठरस्त्रिगुणस्तथा ॥८७॥ 
केशकंथा ललाटश्च व्याघ्रकंथा तथैव च । 
लोचनं भगिनी चैव जालकंथा तथैव च ॥८८॥ 
नटनं बदडिश्चैवं महासूत्रेण संयुताः । 
त्रयोदशविधाश्चैकोरामाराध्यसमुद्भवाः ॥८९॥ 
एते सर्वेऽप्यस्वतंत्रा जाता अपि महात्मना ।
पार्वत्युवाच ।
महाचार्येण संभूताः कथं तेऽप्यस्वतंत्रकाः ।॥९०॥ 
अस्वातंत्र्ये कारणं किमेतद्विस्तरतो वद ।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
अघोराख्यम्मुखोत्पत्तिराहित्येन तथैव च ॥९१॥ 
तदास्यकलशस्यापि कृष्णवर्णमयस्य च । अधिकारित्वराहित्यादनीशास्योद्भवत्वतः ।॥९२॥ भृंगिगोत्राभिधानाच्च स्थूलाष्टाक्षरमंत्रके । 
उपदेष्ट्टत्वराहित्यादृगाद्यागमजातिषु ॥९३॥ अधिकारित्वराहित्याद्वीरशैवालयेषु च । दीक्षालिंगोपदेशादिष्वकर्तारस्ततोऽभवन् ॥९४॥
पार्वत्युवाच ।
कथं कुर्वत्यस्वतंत्रा वीरशैवालयेषु च । 
दीक्षोपदेशनं चैव लिंगधारणपूर्वकम् ।।९५।। 
एतद्विस्तरतो ब्रूहि लोकानुग्रहकांक्षया ।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
त्रयोदशोपसूत्रज्ञा अस्वतंत्रा अपि स्वयम् ॥९६॥ 
महासूत्राधिपतिना चोपदेशादनंतरम् । 
तदनुग्रहतस्तेषां गोत्रप्रवरवर्णकैः ॥९७॥ 
कलशैर्मंत्रदंडाद्यैः कमंडलुसमन्वितैः । 
वीरशैवालयेष्वेते चास्वतंत्राः प्रवर्तकाः ॥९८॥
पार्वत्युवाच ।
त्रयोदशोपसूत्राणामुपदेशोऽभवत्कथम् । 
गुरुः कोऽभूत्साक्षिणः के को मंत्रः कलशश्च कः ।॥९९॥ 
किं बीजं किं विधं लिंगं कस्यां दिशि समाचरेत् । 
इतीशान्या च संपृष्टो भगवानब्रवीद्वचः ॥१००॥
ईश्वर उवाच ।
एकोरामार्यसंभृतास्त्रयोदशविधाश्च ये । 
उपसूत्रज्ञकास्तेषामुपदेशः प्रवक्ष्यते ॥१०१॥ 
एकोरामस्य कृष्णाभमघोरवदनात्मकम् । 
कलशं मध्यमं बीजं शिकारं विलिखेत्ततः ॥१०२॥ 
शिकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं स्थापयेद्बुधः । 
एकोरामंचाधिदैवं मध्ये संभावयेद्गुरुम् ॥१०३॥ 
तत्स्थाने पूर्वदिक्संस्थं शुभ्रं तत्पुरुषात्मकम् । 
कलशं च वकाराख्यं मंत्रबीजं लिखेत्तदा ॥१०४॥ 
वकाराख्ये महाबीजे तत्करीरं न्यसेद्बुधः । 
अधिदैवं पंडितार्य साक्षीभूतं समाचरेत् ।।१०५।। 
तत्स्थाने दक्षिणे सुस्थं पीतेशानमुखात्मकम् । 
कलशं च यकाराख्यं मंत्रबीजं लिखेत्ततः ॥१०६ । 
यकाराख्ये महाबीजे तत्करीरं न्यसेद्बुधः । 
तत्राधिदैवतं विश्वाराध्यं कृत्वा ततः परम् ॥१०७॥ 
तत्स्थाने पश्चिमदिशि युक्तं च हरितं तथा ।
सद्योजातात्मकं वक्त्रं कारयित्वा करीरकम् ॥१०८॥ 
नकारं च विलिख्याथ तस्योपरि करीरकम् । 
विन्यस्य रेवणाराध्यं कृत्वा साक्षिणमव्ययम् ॥१०९॥ 
तत्स्थाने चोत्तरदिशि विशिष्ट वामदेवकम् ।
रक्तवर्णसमायुक्तं मकारं विलिखेत्ततः ॥ ११०॥ 
तस्योपरि न्यसेद्वामदेवात्मककरीरकम् । 
मरुळाराध्यमध्यक्षं साक्षीभूतं समादिशेत् ।।१११॥ 
तथापरं प्रवक्ष्यामि एकोरामार्य लीलया । समुद्भूतोपसूत्रज्ञास्त्रयोदशविधाश्च ते ॥११२॥ 
आगमोक्तप्रकारेण ॐ ऱ्हां ऱ्हीं ऱ्हूं ततः परम् । 
नमः शिवायेति मंत्रमष्टवर्णसमन्वितम् ॥११३॥ 
सूक्ष्मपंचाक्षराख्यं तं मंत्राणा मुत्तमोत्तमम् । 
उपदिष्टाश्च सर्वे त एकोरामाख्यसूरिणा ॥११४॥
नीललिंगं यतो दध्रुरतस्तन्मतवर्तिनः । 
एकोरामार्य एवासावघोरवदनोद्भवः ॥११५।। 
भृंगिगोत्राधिनाथश्च सिंहासनपतिश्च सः । 
एकोरामार्यनामासौ जगद्गुरुतमश्च सः ।।११६॥ 
एभिस्त्रयोदशविधैरुपदिष्टाश्च सर्वशः । 
तेषां च तद्गुरूणां च लिंगधारणकर्मणि ॥११७॥ 
दीक्षोपदेशयोश्चैव विवाहादौ तथैव च । 
चरस्थापनपट्टाभिषेकेषु शुभकर्मसु ।।११८॥ 
निग्रहेऽनुग्रहे चैव आह्वाने च विसर्जने । 
एकोरामाराध्य एव मुख्यकर्ता गुरूत्तमः ॥११९॥ तस्मान्मन्मुखसंजाताः स्वतंत्राश्चेति विश्रुताः ।
तेभ्यो ये च समुत्पन्ना उपसूत्रास्त्रयोदश ॥ १२० ॥ अमुख्यास्तेऽप्यस्वतंत्रा महाचार्यानुगाश्च ते । 
तेभ्यश्चैवोपदिष्टास्तु सामान्या वीरशैवकाः ॥१२१॥ 
ते पंचमा इति ख्याता उपपूर्वास्तथेतरे ॥१२२॥

इति एकोरामार्यदीक्षाप्रकरणम् ।

स्वतंत्रा मुख्यगुरवो महांतश्चेति विश्रुताः ॥१२३॥ 
तथैवमस्वतंत्राणां प्रभेदं वक्तुमर्हसि । 
इत्येवं गिरिजापृष्टो भगवान् भूतभावनः ॥ १२४॥ 
अस्वतंत्रगुरूणां च प्रभेदं वक्तुमारभत् ।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
पूर्व मद्वदनाञ्जातस्तत्पुरुषाद्धेनुकर्णकः ॥ १२५ ॥ 
लीलया चासृजत्सूत्रं मुक्तागुच्छं महत्तरम् ।
स एव पंडिताराध्यो भूत्वा लीलामथाकरोत् ॥ १२६॥ 
तल्लीलया समुत्पन्नान्युपस्सूत्राणि द्वादश । 
गोणीकंथा च दंती च जठरस्त्रिगुणस्तथा ॥१२७॥ 
केशकंथा ललाटश्च व्याघ्रकंथा तथैव च । 
लोचनं भगिनी चैत्र जालकंथा तथैव च ॥१२८॥ 
नटनं बदडिश्चैवं महासूत्रेण संयुताः । 
त्रयोदशविधाश्चैते पंडिताराध्यसंभवाः ॥१२९॥ 
एते सर्वेऽप्यस्वतंत्रा जाता अपि महात्मना ।
पार्वत्युवाच ।
महाचार्येण संभूताः कथं तेऽप्यस्वतंत्रकाः ॥१३०॥ 
अस्वातंत्र्ये कारणं किमेतद्विस्तरतो वद ।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
तत्पुरुषमुखोत्पत्तिराहित्येन तथैव च ॥१३१॥ 
तदास्यकलशस्यापि शुभ्रवर्णमयस्य च । अधिकारित्वराहित्यादनीशास्योद्भवत्वतः ॥१३२॥ वृषगोत्राभिधानाच्च सप्तवर्णान्विते वरे । 
स्थूलपंचाक्षराख्ये च महामंत्रे परात्परे ॥१३३॥ उपदेष्टत्त्रराहित्यादृगाद्यागमजातिषु । अधिकारित्त्रराहित्याद्वीरशैवालयेषु च ॥१३४॥ दीक्षालिंगोपदेशादिष्वकर्तारस्ततोऽभवन् ।
पार्वत्युवाच ।
कथं कुर्वत्यस्वतंत्रा वीरशैवालयेषु च ॥१३५॥ 
दीक्षोपदेशनं चैव लिंगधारणपूर्वकम् । 
एतद्विस्तरतो ब्रूहि लोकानुग्रहकांक्षया ॥१३६॥
ईश्वर उवाच ।
त्रयोदशोपसूत्रज्ञा अस्वतंत्रा अपि स्वयम् । 
महासूत्राधिपतिना चोपदेशादनंतरम् ॥१३७॥ 
तदनुग्रहतस्तेषां गोत्रप्रवरवर्णकैः । 
कलशैर्मंत्रदंडाद्यैः कमंडलुसमन्वितैः ॥१३८॥ 
वीरशैवालयेष्वेते चास्वतंत्राः प्रवर्तकाः ।
पार्वत्युवाच ।
त्रयोदशोपसूत्राणामुपदेशोऽभवत्कथम् ॥१३९॥ 
गुरुः कोऽभूत्साक्षिण: के को मंत्रः कलशश्च कः । 
किं बीजं किंविधं लिंगं कस्यां दिशि समाचरेत् ॥१४०॥ 
इतीशान्या च संपृष्टो भगवानब्रवीद्वचः ।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
पंडिताराध्यसंजातास्त्रयोदशविधाश्च ये ॥१४१॥ 
उपसूत्रज्ञकास्तेषामुपदेशः प्रवक्ष्यते । 
पंडितार्यस्य शुभ्राभं तत्पुरुषमुखात्मकम् ॥१४२॥ 
कलशं तु वकाराख्यं मध्ये बीजं लिखेत्सुधीः । 
वकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं तं न्यसेत्ततः ॥१४३॥ 
अधिदैवं पंडितार्यं मध्ये संभावयेद्गुरुम् । 
तत्स्थाने प्राक्दिशिस्थ च पीतवर्णविशिष्टकम् ॥१४४।॥ विश्वाराध्यात्मकं तत्र यकारं विलिखेत्ततः । 
यकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं तत्र विन्यसेत् ॥१४५॥ 
तत्राधिदैवतं विश्वाराध्यं कृत्वाथ साक्षिणम् । 
तत्स्थाने दक्षिणोपेतं सद्योजात मुखात्मकम् ।।१४६ 
नकारं च समालिख्य तस्योपरि करीरकम् । 
विन्यसेद्रेवणाराध्यं कृत्वा साक्षिणमव्ययम् ॥१४७॥
तत्स्थाने पश्चिमदिशि विशिष्टं वामदेवकम् । 
रक्तवर्णसमायुक्तं मकारं विलिखेत्ततः ॥१४८॥ 
तस्योपरि न्यसेद्वामदेवात्मककरीरकम् । 
मरुळाराध्यमध्यक्षं साक्षीभूतं समादिशेत् ॥ १४९॥ 
तत्स्थाने चोत्तरे कृष्णमघोरवदनात्मकम् । 
उत्तमोत्तमतायुक्तं कलशं विन्यसेत्ततः ॥१५०॥ 
शिकाराख्यं महामंत्रबीजं च विलिखेत्ततः । 
शिकाराख्ये महाबीजे तत्करीरं न्यसेद्बुधः ॥१५१॥ 
अधिदैवं चैकरामं साक्षीभूतं समाचरेत् । 
ततः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि पंडिताराध्यलीलया ।।१५२॥ समुद्भूतोपसूत्रज्ञास्त्रयोदशविधाश्चये । 
उपदिष्टाश्च सर्वेऽपि पंडिताराध्यसूरिणा ॥१५३॥ 
वज्ज्रलिंगं ततो द‌ध्रुस्तन्मतालंबनाश्च ते । 
त्रयोदशानामेतेषां तत्पुरुषसुखोद्भवः ॥१५४।। 
वृषगोत्राधिनाथश्च सिंहासनपतिश्च सः । 
पंडिताराध्यसन्नामा जगद्गुरुतमश्च सः ॥१५५।। एभिस्त्रयोदशविधैरुपदिष्टाश्च सर्वशः । 
तेषां च तद्गुरूणां च लिंगधारणकर्मणि ॥१५६॥ 
दीक्षोपदेशयोश्चैव विवाहादौ तथैव च । 
चरस्थापनपट्टाभिषेकेषु शुभकर्मसु ॥१५७॥ 
निग्रहेऽनुग्रहे चैव आह्वाने च विसर्जने । 
पंडिताराध्य एवासौ मुख्यकर्ता गुरूत्तमः ॥१५८॥ 
तस्मान्मन्मुखसंजाताः स्वतंत्राश्चेति विश्रुताः । 
तेभ्य एव समुत्पन्ना उपसूत्रास्त्रयोदश ॥१५९॥ अमुख्यास्तेऽप्यस्वतंत्रा महाचार्यानुगाश्च ते । 
तेभ्यश्चैवोपदिष्टास्तु सामान्या वीरशैवकाः ॥ १६०॥
ते पंचमा इति ख्याता उपपूर्वास्तथेतरे ॥१६१॥

इति पंडिताराध्यदीक्षाप्रकरणम् ।

[123] Pārvatī says, “O Bhagavan, the five pīṭhādhipatis that you have described—you say they are highly independent and prominent gurus;

[124] then, in the same manner, please kindly explain to me the distinctions of those who are not independent.” After Pārvatī asked in this way, the Supreme Lord, the creator of all beings,

[125] began to explain the distinctions of the dependent gurus. Īśvara says, “First, from my Tatpuruṣa face, Dhenukarṇa was born.

[126] By his natural divine play, he produced a great sūtra named Muktāguccha. Later, he became Paṇḍitārādhya and engaged in divine play,

[127–129] and through that play twelve upasūtras were produced: Goṇīkantha, Dantī, Jaṭhara, Triguṇa, Keśakantha, Lalāṭa, Vyāghrakantha, Locana, Bhaginī, Jālakantha, Naṭana, and Baḍadī. These twelve, along with the Mahāsūtra named Muktāguccha, make a total of thirteen.

[130] Although all these have originated from the great being ( Dhenukarṇa/Paṇḍitārādhya ) , they should be understood as dependent.” Pārvatī asks, “Though they have originated from the Mahāchārya, how are they not independent?

[131] And what is the reason for their dependence? Please explain all this to me in detail.”

[131–135] Īśvara says, “They are not directly born from the Tatpuruṣa face, and they also do not have authority over the white-colored kalasha of that Tatpuruṣa face. Since they are not born from the mouth of Parameśvara, they are not entitled to impart the great mantra of the 7 syllabled sthula Pañcākṣarī of the Vṛṣabha gotra, which is supreme. Likewise, as they have no authority over the Vedas and Āgamas such as the Ṛgveda, they are not entitled to perform dīkṣā or liṅgopadeśa in the houses of Vīraśaivas.”

[135–136] Pārvatī asks, “If they are not independent, then how do they perform initiation with liṅga-wearing and give instruction in the houses of Vīraśaivas? O Bhagavan, please explain this to me in detail for the welfare of people.”

[137–139] Īśvara says, “Although the thirteen upasūtra-knowers are not themselves independent, after receiving instruction from the lord of the Mahāsūtra ( Dhenukarṇa/Paṇḍitārādhya ), by his grace they conduct religious rites such as initiation and instruction in the houses of Vīraśaivas along with gotra, pravara, varṇa, kalasha, staff, mantra, and water-pot.”

[139–140] Pārvatī asks, “How is instruction given to these thirteen upasūtras? Who is their guru? Who are the witnesses? What is their mantra? What kalasha, bīja-mantra, and liṅga do they have? And what are their directions?”

[141] After Pārvatī asked in this manner, Bhagavan Parameśvara began to explain to her.

[141–143] Īśvara says, “I shall explain the method of instruction for the thirteen upasūtra-knowers who originated from Paṇḍitārādhya. Paṇḍitārādhya has the Tatpuruṣa aspect, a white-colored kalasha, and the bīja-mantra ‘va’ is to be written. The kalasha should be established at the place of this great bīja-mantra, and the presiding deity, Guru Paṇḍitārādhya, should be invoked in the center.

[144–146] To his east, there should be a yellow-colored kalasha of the Viśvārādhya aspect, and the bīja-mantra ‘ya’ should be written; the kalasha should be established there, and the presiding deity Viśvārādhya should be made the witness.

[146–147] To his south, there should be a green-colored kalasha of the Sadyojāta aspect, and the bīja-mantra ‘na’ should be written; the kalasha should be established there, and the presiding deity Revaṇārādhya should be made the witness.

[148–149] Then, to his west, there should be a red-colored kalasha of the Vāmadeva aspect, and the bīja-mantra ‘ma’ should be written; the kalasha should be established there, and the presiding deity Maruḷārādhya should be made the witness.

[150–152] To his north, there should be a black/dark blue-colored kalasha of the Aghora aspect, and the bīja-mantra ‘śi’ should be written; the kalasha should be established there, and the presiding deity Ekorāmārādhya should be made the witness.

[152–153] Further, O Pārvatī, I shall describe the divine play of Paṇḍitārādhya. From his play, thirteen upasūtras were produced, and Paṇḍitārādhya himself imparted instruction to all of them.

[154] Paṇḍitārādhya has worn a Vajra-liṅga, and accordingly, those who follow his doctrine also wear a Vajra-liṅga. These thirteen upasūtra-knowers are said to have originated from the aspect of Tatpuruṣa face.

[155] The primal lord and throne-holder of the Vṛṣabha gotra, Paṇḍitārādhya, is the supreme Jagadguru.

[156–158] From these thirteen, all kinds of instruction are given. However, among all these gurus, at the time of liṅga-dhāraṇa, when initiation or instruction is to be given, at the time of marriage, at the installation of caramurtis or consecration of pontiffs, during auspicious rites, and when granting restraint or grace, and at the time of invocation and dismissal, the one born from the Tatpuruṣa face—Paṇḍitārādhya Guru alone—is the principal performer.

[159–161] Therefore, only those who are directly born from my faces are called independent; they alone are independent. Those thirteen upasūtra-knowers who have originated from them are not principal or independent in any function, but merely followers of the Mahāchārya. Those Vīraśaivas who receive initiation from them are considered ordinary. These are called Pañcamas, and those who arise from them are called Upapañcamas.

Thus ends the section on the initiation of Paṇḍitārādhya's Pitha.

विश्वाराध्यार्यमध्यक्षं मध्ये संभावयेद्गुरुम् ।।१८३॥ 
तत्स्थाने पूर्वदिक्संस्थं हरिद्वर्णविराजितम् । 
सद्योजातात्मकं तत्र नकारं विलिखेत्ततः ॥१८४॥ 
नकाराख्ये महाबीजे तत्करीरं न्यसेद्बुधः । 
तत्राधिदैवतं चैव रेवणाराध्यनामकम् ॥१८५॥ 
तत्स्थाने दक्षिणोपेतं रक्तवर्णविराजितम् । 
वामदेवात्मकं तत्र मकारं विलिखेत्ततः ॥१८६॥ 
मकाराख्ये महाबीजे कलशं विन्यसेत्ततः । 
तत्राधिदैवतं कृत्वा मरुळाराध्यनामकम् ॥१८७।। 
साक्षीभूतं विदित्वा तं तथैव च ततः परम् ।
तत्स्थाने पश्चिमोपेतं कृष्णवर्णविराजितम् ॥१८८॥ 
अघोरास्यात्मकं तत्र शिकारं विलिखेत्ततः । 
शिकाराख्ये मंत्रबीजे कलशं स्थापयेत्सुधीः ॥१८९॥ 
तत्राधिदैवतं चैव एकोरामाख्यकं परम् । 
साक्षीभूताधिदैवं तं निर्माय च ततः परम् ॥१९०॥ 
तत्स्थाने चोत्तरोपेतं तत्पुरुषम्मुखात्मकम् । 
वज्रकांतिसमोपेतं कलशं पंडिताभिधम् ॥१९१॥ 
वकारं च लिखित्वा तु तस्योपरि करीरकम् । 
विन्यस्य पंडिताराध्यं भावयेत्साक्षिकं गुरुम् ।।१९२।। 
ततः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि विश्वाराध्यस्य लीलया । समुद्भूतोपसूत्रज्ञास्त्रयोदशविधाश्च ते ॥१९३॥ 
आगमोक्तविधानेन षडक्षरसमन्वितम् । 
मूलपंचाक्षरं मंत्रमुपदिष्टाः पृथक् पृथक् ॥१९४॥ 
विश्वाराध्येनगुरुणा ज्योतिर्लिंगमदीधरन् । 
अथ सर्वोपसूत्रज्ञास्तन्मतालंबनाश्च ते ॥१९५॥ 
पंचवर्णश्च कंबालो वृषभो दशवक्त्रकः । 
जरत्कंथा पंचमुखो गुहाम्रो गोचरश्च सः ॥ १९६॥ 
गगनं मुसली चेति लगुडः शिथिली तथा । 
पाशुपत्यं महासूत्रसंयुक्तास्ते त्रयोदश ॥१९७॥ 
एवं भेदवतामेषामूर्ध्वेशानास्यसंभवः । 
स्कंदगोत्राधिनाथश्च महासिंहासनाग्रणीः ॥१९८॥ 
विश्वाराध्य इति ख्यातो जगद्गुरुतमश्च सः । एभिस्त्रयोदशविधैरुपदिष्टाश्च सर्वशः ॥ १९९॥ 
तेषां चैव गुरूणां च लिंगधारणकर्मणि । 
दीक्षोपदेशयोश्चैव विवाहादौ तथैव च ॥२००॥ चरस्थापनपट्टाभिषेकेषु शुभकर्मसु । 
निग्रहेऽनुग्रहे चैत्र आह्वाने च विसर्जने ॥२०१॥ 
ईशानवदनोद्भूतो विश्वाराध्यश्च मुख्यकः । 
स्वतंत्रो गुरुराख्यात आचार्योऽभूद्धरातले ॥२०२॥ तस्मान्मन्मुखसंजाताः स्वतंत्राश्चेति विश्रुताः । 
तेभ्य एव समुत्पन्ना उपसूत्रास्त्रयोदश ॥ २०३॥ 
अमुख्यास्तेऽप्यस्वतंत्रा महाचार्यानुगाश्च ते । 
तेभ्यश्चैवोपदिष्टास्तु सामान्या वीरशैवकाः ॥ २०४॥ 
ते पंचमा इति ख्याता उपपूर्वास्तथेतरे ॥२०५॥

इति विश्वाराध्यदीक्षाप्रकरणम् ।

[162] Pārvatī says, “O Lord of gods, giver of bliss to the entire universe, O ruler of the world!

[163] The five lords of the thrones are independent and principal performers, and the twelve (upasūtra-knowers) produced from their divine play are dependent.

[164] Therefore, please kindly explain to me the distinctions of those who are not independent.” After Pārvatī asked in this manner, the Supreme Lord, the creator of all beings,

[165] began to explain the distinctions of the dependent gurus. Īśvara says, “First, from my Īśāna face, Viśvakarna was born.

[166] By his natural divine play, he produced a great sūtra named Pañcavarṇa. Later, he became Viśvārādhya and engaged in divine play.

[167–169] Through that divine play, twelve upasūtras were produced: Kambala, Vṛṣabha, Daśānana, Jaratkantha, Pañcavaktra, Guhāgraka, Gocara, Gagana, Musalī, Laguḍa, Śithila, and Pāśupatya. These twelve, together with the Pañcavarṇa Mahāsūtra, make a total of thirteen. Although all these have originated from the Mahāchārya, they are not independent or principal in any ritual act.”

[170] Pārvatī asks, “Though they have originated from the Mahāchārya, how are they not independent? And what is the reason for their dependence? Please explain all this to me in detail.”

[171–174] Īśvara says, “O Pārvatī, since they are not directly born from the Īśāna face, they do not have authority over the yellow-colored kalasha. Since they are not born from the mouth of Īśvara, and as they declare the Skanda gotra, they are not entitled to impart the mula Pañcākṣarī Mahāmantra consisting of six syllables. Likewise, as they have no authority over the Vedas and Āgamas such as the Ṛgveda, they are not entitled to perform dīkṣā or liṅgopadeśa in the houses of Vīraśaivas.”

[175–176] Pārvatī asks, “If they are not independent, then how do they perform initiation with liṅga-wearing and give instruction in the houses of Vīraśaivas? O Bhagavan, please explain this to me in detail.”

[176–178] Īśvara says, “Although these thirteen upasūtra-knowers are themselves dependent, after receiving instruction from the lord of the Mahāsūtra, by his grace they conduct activities in Vīraśaiva temples—along with gotra, pravara, varṇa, kalasha, staff, mantra, and water-pot—even though they are not independent.”

[179–180] Pārvatī says, “How is instruction given to these thirteen upasūtras? Who is their guru? Who are the witnesses? What are their mantras? What is the color of their kalasha? What is their bīja-mantra? What type of liṅga do they have? And in which direction should this rite be performed?” After Pārvatī asked thus, Īśvara began to explain.

[181–183] Īśvara says, “These dependent ones have originated from Viśvārādhya and have thirteen divisions. I shall explain their method of instruction. Guru Viśvārādhya is golden-yellow in color and is born from the Īśāna face. Therefore, placing a kalasha in the center, one should write the bīja syllable ‘ya’ upon it. This ‘ya’ syllable is the Mahābīja mantra. The learned should place the kalasha upon it and establish Guru Viśvārādhya in the central, principal position.

[184–185] In the east, one should write the green-colored Sadyojāta mantra in the form of ‘na’; placing the kalasha upon that bīja, one should understand the presiding deity there to be Revaṇārādhya.

[186–187] On the southern side, one should write the red-colored ‘ma’ of the Vāmadeva form; placing the kalasha upon that bīja, one should establish Maruḷārādhya as the presiding deity and understand him as the witness.

[188–190] Then, on the western side, one should write the black/dark blue-colored ‘śi’ of the Aghora aspect; placing the kalasha upon that bīja, one should establish Guru Ekorāma as the presiding deity and make him the witness.

[191–192] On the northern side, one should place a kalasha of the Tatpuruṣa form, having a vajra-like color, and write the syllable ‘va’; placing the kalasha upon it, one should establish Paṇḍitārādhya as the presiding deity and make him the witness.

[193–194] Further, I shall describe the next part. By the mere divine play of Viśvārādhya, these thirteen types of upasūtra-knowers were produced, and according to the Āgamic method, he imparted to them the mula Pañcākṣarī mantra consisting of six syllables in various ways.

[195] By the grace of Guru Viśvārādhya, all these followers adopted his doctrine and began to wear the Jyotirliṅga.

[196–197] The names of the Mahāsūtras of these thirteen are as follows: Pañcavarṇa, Kambala, Vṛṣabha, Yaśavaktraka, Jaratkantha, Pañcamukha, Guhāgra, Gocara, Gagana, Musalī, Laguḍa, Śithilī, and Pāśupatya.

[198–199] Among these divisions, the one born from the upward Īśāna face, belonging to the Skanda gotra, the chief lord of the great  throne ( simhasan )—the supreme emperor—is Viśvārādhya, the greatest Jagadguru. He imparted instruction to these thirteen upasūtra-knowers, and thereafter they instructed their own lineages of disciples.

[200–202] At the time of liṅga-dhāraṇa, when initiation or instruction is to be given, at the time of marriage, and during auspicious rites such as installation of caramurtis and consecration, as well as during acts of restraint, grace, invocation, and dismissal, at all such times, the Guru Viśvārādhya—born from the Īśāna face—is the principal deity. He is independent and became renowned throughout the world as an Āchārya.

[203–205] Therefore, those who are born from my faces are known as independent. From them arose these thirteen upasūtra-knowers. These are secondary (of lesser status), dependent, and act according to the command of the Mahāchārya. Those who receive instruction from them are ordinary Vīraśaivas. These are known as Pañcamas, and others arising from them are known as Upapañcamas.

Thus ends the section on the initiation of Viśvārādhya's pitha

पार्वत्युवाच ।
गुरवस्ते पंचविधास्त्वदाननसमुद्भवाः । 
तेषां गोत्रं पृथक् चैत्र तेषां वर्णादिकं पृथक् ॥२०६॥ 
तेषां कमंडलुश्चैत्र तेपां दंडः पृथक् पृथक् । 
तेषां च कलशं चैत्र मंत्रबीजं पृथक् पृथक् ॥२०७॥ 
तलीलया समुद्भूता उपसूत्रास्त्रयोदश । 
तेषां प्रभेदं च तथा तैस्तैः कार्यैः पृथक् पृथक् ॥२०८।। इत्येतत्सर्वमाख्यातं प्रमेयं विदितं मया । 
सामान्यवीरशैवानां वीरशैवक्रियावताम् ॥२०९॥ 
एते त्रयोदशविधा उपसूत्रज्ञकाश्च ये । 
वयं गुरव इत्येवं संवदंत्यभिमानतः ॥२१०॥ 
तेषां गुरुत्वं सर्वेष्वप्यागमेषु प्रमाणितम् । 
कथं प्राप्तं वद ब्रह्मन् देव देव जगत्पते ॥२११॥ 
इति शैलात्मजापृष्टो भगवानब्रवीद्वचः ।
ईश्वर उवाच ।
पंचानां च महार्याणां जाता ये लीलया प्रिये ॥२१२॥ 
ते सर्वे वीरशैवानां दीक्षायां लिंगधारणे । 
उपदेशे विवाहे च गौणतो गुरवः स्मृताः ॥२१३॥ 
गुरूणां लक्षणं चैव शिक्षारक्षणयोस्तथा । 
आह्वाने च विसर्गे च यः स्वतंत्रः स वै गुरुः ॥२१४॥ 
आह्वाने च विसर्गे चाप्यसमर्थाश्च ते परम् । 
सर्वेषां ब्राह्मणादीनां यथा गेहे पुरोहिताः ॥२१५॥ 
तद्वत्सामान्यशैवानां गृहेष्वेते पुरोहिताः । 
तेषां ते मूलगुरवः पीठाधिपतयश्च ये ॥ २१६॥ 
न तेषां सत्यशीलानामुपमानाः पुरोहिताः । 
पंचानां च महार्याणां तच्छिष्याणां तथैव हि ॥२१७॥ 
सामान्यभावतः पूजां ये कुर्वंति नराधमाः । 
पूजाकर्ता पूजितश्च नरकानेव विंदति ।।२१८॥ 
मत्पंचवदनोद्भूताः सर्व एव गुरूत्तमाः । 
तत्सृष्टानां च सर्वेषां तत्सामर्थ्य कथं भवेत् ॥२१९।। ब्रह्मत्रिष्णुमहेशाद्या मदाज्ञाधारकाश्च ते । 
हित्वा मदाज्ञां सृष्ट्यादिकर्तृत्वं च कथं भवेत् ॥२२०॥ 
लोके सर्वपतंगानां पक्षित्वं वर्ततेऽनघे । 
एतावता खगपतेः समानाः करटा नहि ॥२२१॥ 
सर्वेषां मृगजातीनां मृगत्वं वर्तते शिवे । 
कंठीरवस मार्जालः समो न हि महीध्रजे ॥२२२॥
लोके सर्वशिलानां च शिलात्वं वर्तते ऽबिके । 
चिंतामणिः शर्कराया लवणं न कदाचन ॥२२३॥ 
राज्ञां राजसुतानां च शिक्षारक्षणकर्मसु । 
राजैव हि समर्थः स्यात्पुत्राणां न कदाचन ॥२२४॥ 
सर्वेषां भूरुहाणां च वृक्षत्वं वर्ततेऽगजे । 
तथापि कल्पवृक्षस्य बर्नूरास्तु सभा न हि ॥२२५॥ 
तथा गौणगुरूणां च प्रभावः शिष्यजातिषु । 
न कदाचिन्मया दृष्टो न श्रुतः शैलकन्यके ॥ २२६॥ 
तस्मात्पंचविधाचार्याः पंच पीठाधिदेवताः । 
पंचसिंहासनाधीशा जगद्गुरुतमाश्चते ॥२२७॥ पंचकैरेभिरुद्भूतास्तत्तत्सुत्रानुसारिणः । 
पंचसृष्टिविधाश्चैते पंचकानां महात्मनाम् ॥२२८॥ कलशैर्दंडमंत्राद्यैगोत्रप्रवरवर्णकैः । 
एतादृशैर्लक्षणैस्तु समुपेतं स्वसूत्रपम् ॥२२९॥ 
गुरुं संभाव्य त्वन्योन्यैः साक्षीकृत्य ततः परम् । 
दीक्षोपदेशनं चैव लिंगधारणपूर्वकम् ॥२३० 
तत्तन्मुद्रानुसारेण कुर्वंत्येते महीतले । 
तत्तच्छिष्यसमूहानां तत्तज्ज्ञानानुसारिणाम् ॥२३१॥ 
पंचपीठाधिदेवानां ये जानंति समानताम् । 
ते गर्दभाश्च संत्रोक्ता ज्ञानशून्यत्वतः शिवे ।।२३२। 
तस्मात्तस्माच्च गिरिजे पंचाननसमुद्भवाः। 
मदादिसर्वलोकानां जगद्गुरुवरोत्तमाः ।॥ २३३॥ 
तस्मात्स्वतंत्रकर्तारस्तञ्जाताश्चोपसूत्रकाः । 
अमुख्यास्तेप्यस्वतंत्राः सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् ॥२३४॥

इत्यस्वतंत्रगुरुनिरूपणम् समाप्तम्.

[206–207] Pārvatī says, “O Īśvara, the five types of gurus born from your faces are well known. They have distinct gotras, different varṇas, their water-pots are different, their staffs are different, their kalashas are different, and their bīja-mantras are also different.

[208–209] The thirteen types of upasūtra-knowers produced through their divine play are also distinct, and their castes and functions are different. You have explained all this to me, and I have understood it. Now, among the other Vīraśaivas who follow the conduct of the Vīraśaiva path,

[210–211] these thirteen types of upasūtra-knowers speak proudly, saying ‘we are gurus.’ How have they obtained the status of guru in all the Āgamas? Please explain this. You are the knower of Brahman, the God of all gods, and the Lord of the three worlds.”

[212–213] After Pārvatī, the daughter of Himālaya, asked in this way, Īśvara said, “O beloved, these thirteen types of upasūtra-knowers who have arisen from the divine play of the five Mahāchāryas are regarded as gurus only in a secondary sense during occasions such as initiation, liṅga-dhāraṇa, instruction, and marriage among Vīraśaivas.

[214] The primary definition of a guru is one who possesses complete independence in acts such as discipline, protection, invocation, and dismissal.

[215–216] At the time of invocation and dismissal, they ( pancama and upapancama gurus ) are entirely incapable. Just as in the houses of all Brāhmaṇas there are subordinate teachers (upādhyāyas), similarly, in the houses of ordinary Vīraśaivas, these are dependent upādhyāyas. Their pīṭhādhipatis ( mahacaryas/pancacaryas ) are the original gurus.

[217–218] These truthful-natured pīṭhādhipatis ( mahacaryas/pancacaryas ) cannot be equated with such upādhyāyas ( pancama and upapancama gurus ). Those inferior people who worship the five Mahāchāryas and their disciples as equal—both the worshipper and the one who receives such worship go to hell.

[219–220] The five who are born from my five faces ( mahacaryas/pancacaryas ) are all supreme gurus . How can those produced by them attain the same qualification? Even Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara act according to my command; without my command, how can they perform acts such as creation?

[221] O sinless one, just as all birds in the world may be called ‘birds,’ yet a crow cannot be compared with Garuḍa,

[222] and all animals may be called ‘animals,’ yet a cat cannot be compared with a lion,

[223] and all stones may be called ‘stones,’ yet a piece of gravel cannot be compared with the wish-fulfilling gem (cintāmaṇi),

[224] and though both a king and a prince may be called ‘king,’ only the king can punish and protect the subjects, not the prince, and though all trees may be called ‘trees,’ the pārijāta tree cannot be compared with a babul tree—

[226–227] in the same way, O Pārvatī, I have neither seen nor heard that the power of a primary guru exists in subordinate gurus. Therefore, the five Āchāryas, the heads of the five pīṭhas, the lords of the five thrones, are the supreme Jagadgurus.

[228–229] Those who have arisen from this group of five gurus, and who act according to their respective sūtras, are the ones who carry out the fivefold creation of the five Mahātmyas. With characteristics such as kalasha, staff, mantra, gotra, pravara, and varṇa,

[230–231] they invoke their respective sūtra-lords as gurus, establish others as witnesses, and after first performing liṅga-dhāraṇa, they carry out initiation and instruction according to their respective marks; thus their dependent disciples conduct themselves in the world.

[231–232] Those people who equate their respective disciples and their communities, who act according to their level of knowledge, with the deities of the five pīṭhas—O Pārvatī, such people, having no wisdom at all, should be regarded as fools.

[233–234] Therefore, O Pārvatī, those five pīṭhādhipatis born from my five faces are the supreme Jagadgurus of all worlds, along with myself. Hence, they are independent performers, and those upasūtra-knowers produced from them are secondary and dependent—this statement of mine is true."

Thus ends the description of the dependent gurus.

स्थूलपंचाक्षरो मंत्रो सप्तवर्णसमन्वितः ॥४७॥ 
ॐ ऱ्हां ऱ्हीं नमः शिवाय सर्वोत्कृष्टमिदं स्मृतम् । एतादृशमहामंत्रस्योपदेशेन राजितः ॥४८॥ 
सोऽत्याश्रमी गृहस्थः स्यादिष्टलिंगार्चने रतः । 
एतैश्च लक्षणैर्युक्तः स्मरारिः पंचमस्तथा ॥४९

तस्य गर्भे समुद्भूता ऋतुद्विगुणपंचमाः । 
तस्य तस्य पृथङ्नाम प्रवदामि वरानने ॥५१॥
सहस्रशीर्षः पीतांगो नगमालो निराशनः । 
यमद्युतिश्च सप्तांगो लतांगो मृत्युनाशनः ॥५२॥ 
अतनुर्घोटवक्त्रश्च नीरोगश्च भवाह्वयः । 
एतैर्नामभिर्युक्ताश्च विश्रुता उपपंचमाः ।।५३।। 
एतेषां पंचमानां च स्मरारेश्च समुद्भवः । 
गुरोर्गोत्रं च तेषां वै गोत्रं ज्ञेयं वरानने ।॥५४॥ 
त्यक्त्वा स्वगोत्रमन्यस्मिन्कुर्यादुद्वाहमद्रिजे । 
स्वस्मिन्कदाचित्संबंधो न कार्यश्च मनीषिभिः ॥५५॥
प्रमादाद्यः प्रकुर्वीत संबंधं स तु दोषभाक् । 
वेदारिपंचमाख्यस्य स्कंदगोत्रं हि गीयते ॥५६॥ 
तच्छाखा विश्वकर्णाख्या प्रवरः पंचकाक्षरः । 
तत्सूत्रं पंचवर्ण च मूलवणे यकारकम् ॥५७॥
सौवर्णश्चापि कलशो विश्वाराध्यो गुरुः स्मृतः । 
षडक्षरो महामंत्रो मूलमंत्रः स एव हि ॥५८॥ 
ॐ नमः शिवाय मनुः सर्वमंत्रेषु चोत्तमः । एतादृशमहामंत्रस्योपदशेन राजितः ॥५९॥ 
सोऽत्याश्रमी गृहस्थः स्यादिष्टलिंगेन संयुतः । 
एतैश्च लक्षणैर्युक्तो वेदारिः पंचमस्तथा ॥६०॥ 
तत्सूत्रे च समुत्पन्ना द्वादश हयुपपंचमाः । 
ईशानाख्यम्मुखाद्देवि वेदारिः समजायत ॥६१॥ 
तस्य गर्भे समुद्भुता द्वादशैवोपपंचमाः । 
तस्य तस्य पृथङ्नाम वदामि शृणु मत्प्रिये ॥६२॥ 
पश्चादृग्विश्वपुष्टश्च गोमुखो गिरिवक्त्रकः । सुवर्णनखरोऽञ्जांघ्रिर्दशाननविषाननौ ॥६३॥ 
उग्रदेहः शतपदः सहस्रस्कंध एव च । 
त्रिमुखस्कंधविख्यातो द्वादश हयुपपंचमाः ॥६४॥ 
एते वै पंचमासर्वे वेदारेर्गर्भसंभवाः । 
गुरोर्गोत्रं च तेषां वै गोत्रं ज्ञेयं वरानने ॥६५॥ 
हित्वा स्वगोत्रमन्यस्मिन्कर्तव्यं पाणिपीडनम् । 
स्वगोत्रे चैव संबंधो न कार्यः सुमनीषिभिः ॥६६॥ 
प्रमादाद्यः प्रकुर्वीत संबंधं स तु दोषभाक् । 
स्वगोत्रकं गुरुं त्यक्त्वा चान्यगोत्रः गुरोरपि ॥६७॥ 
यः कुर्वीतोद्वाहविधिं स चांडालो भविष्यति । 
तस्मात्कारणतो देवि स्वाचार्येण महात्मना ॥६८॥ 
कार्य वैवाहिकं कर्म श्लाघ्यं ज्ञेयं महात्मभिः । 
प्रमादाद्यः प्रकुर्वीत स्वस्वगोत्रे विवाहकम् ॥६९।।
स स्वपुत्रीसमायोगाद्‌गोत्रसांकर्यकारकः । 
तत्र पंचविधाः संति गुरूणां कलशाः प्रिये ॥७०॥ 
सूत्रं वर्णस्तथा शाखा मंत्रप्रवरकावपि । 
स्वस्वगोत्रानुसारेण सर्व ज्ञेयं मनीषिभिः ॥७१॥ 
तेषां संस्थापनविधिं वक्ष्ये शास्त्रविनिश्चितम् । 
चरंति पंचप्रणवाः स्वस्वगोत्रानुसारतः ॥७२॥ 
मखारेर्गोत्रजातानां विवाहोऽपि यदा भवेत् । 
तदा तत्प्रणवं मध्ये नकारं स्थापयेद्बुधः ॥७३॥ 
मकारं पूर्वतः कृत्वा शिकारं दक्षिणे न्यसेत् ।
वकारं पश्चिमे कुर्याद्यकारं चोत्तरे न्यसेत् ॥७४॥
कालारेर्गोत्रजातानां विवाहोऽपि यदा भवेत् । 
तदा मकारं मध्ये तु प्रणवं स्थापयेद्बुधः ॥७५॥ 
शिकारं पूर्वदेशे तु वकारं दक्षिणे न्यसेत् । 
यकारं पश्चिमे कुर्यान्नकारं चोत्तरे न्यसेत् । ७६।। 
पुरारेर्गोत्रजातानां विवाहोऽपि यदा भवेत् । 
तदा तत्प्रणवं मध्ये शिकारं विन्यसेद्बुधः ॥७७॥ 
वकारं पूर्वतः कृत्वा यकारं दक्षिणे न्यसेत् । 
नकारं पश्चिमे कृत्वा मकारं चोत्तरे न्यसेत् ॥७८॥
स्मरारेर्गोत्रजातानां विवाहोऽपि यदा भवेत् । 
तदा तत्प्रणवं मध्ये वकारं विन्यसेद्बुधः ॥७९॥
यकारं पूर्वतः कृत्वा नकारं दक्षिणे न्यसेत् । 
मकारं पश्चिमे कृत्वा शिकारं चोत्तरे न्यसेत् ॥८०॥ वेदारेगर्गोत्रजातानां विवाहोऽपि यदा भवेत् । 
तदा तत्प्रणवं मध्ये यकारं स्थापयेद्बुधः ॥८१ । 
नकारं पूर्वतः कृत्वा मकारं दक्षिणे न्यसेत् । 
शिकारं पश्चिमे कृत्वा वकारं चोत्तरे न्यसेत् ॥८२॥ 
मखारेश्च नकारोऽयं कालारेश्च मकारकः । 
पुरारेश्च शिकारोऽयं स्मरारेश्च वकारकः ।॥८३॥ 
यकारश्चैव वेदारेः प्रणवाः परिकीर्तिताः ।
यस्यां दिशि यः प्रणव: सा दिक् तस्य विनिर्दिशेत् ॥84॥ 
दिक् प्रधानं न चैतेषां प्रणवेनैव निर्णयः । 
एवं शास्त्रोक्तविधिना पंचकान्कलशानपि ॥८५॥ 
संस्थाप्य फलनैवेद्यैर्दशधा बंधितैस्तथा । 
सद‌क्षिणैः सतांबूलैः परिपूज्य यथाविधि ॥८६॥ 
पार्वत्युवाच । 
पंचैव कलशास्तत्र स्थापितव्या हि शंकर ।
किमर्थ दशधा तेषां नैवेद्यादि विनिक्षिपेत् ॥८७॥ 
ईश्वर उवाच । 
पंचाचार्याः पंचविधा वृत्त्याचार्याश्च पंचधा । 
एवं दशविधानां तु भागश्च परिकल्पितः ॥८८।। 
तस्माद्दशविधं तत्र फलनैवेद्यकं न्यसेत् । 
पंच पूर्णानि निक्षिप्य तदर्थं पंचधा क्षिपेत् ॥८९॥
पूर्णभागं महाचार्या आहरेयुर्यथाक्रमम् । 
उपसूत्रैः समायुक्ताश्चैवमेव विनिर्णयः ॥९०॥
तदर्धं चैव गृण्हीयुर्वृत्त्याचार्यास्ततः परम् । 
एकस्य भागमेकश्च गृहीतुं नैव चार्हति ॥९१॥ 
बलादपि च गृण्हीयात्समानस्कंधता भवेत् । 
तेन दोषफलं भुक्त्वा नरकानेव विंदति ॥९२॥ 
वृत्त्याचार्यपदार्थं तु महाचार्यो यदा हरेत् । 
तदा तस्यैव नगजे न्यूनता भवति ध्रुवम् ॥९३॥ 
एवं शास्त्रोक्तविधिना पंचकान्कलशानपि । 
प्राणप्रतिष्ठां कृत्वा तान्ब्रह्ममंत्रैर्न्यसेद्बुधः॥९४॥ 

इति वीरशैवब्राह्मणपंचमहाचार्यपंचमोत्पत्तिप्रकरणं समाप्तम् ।
data.english:
[1] Īśvara says to Pārvatī, “O Pārvatī, from my Īśāna face was born Pañcavaktra (five-faced) Gaṇeśvara. From his five faces were born five sons of pure conduct.”
[2] Pārvatī asked, “From which face did each one arise? What are their names? What are their respective sūtras? Tell me.”
[3] “O compassionate Lord, also explain in detail their gotras, branches, and pravaras.”
[4] Īśvara says, “From my upper face was born Pañcavaktra Gaṇeśvara. He is beyond varṇa and āśrama ( ativarnasrami ) and is supreme in the Vīraśaiva doctrine.”
[5] “From his five faces arose five Pañcamas. I will explain their gotras and all other details.”
[6] “Since they are born from the five faces of Pañcavaktra Gaṇeśvara, they are also superior. These Pañcamas are my dear devotees and are greatest among all varṇas.”
[7] “Their conduct is of ativarnasrama i.e. beyond varṇa and āśrama, and they are always engaged in the worship of the Śiva-liṅga. O Mahādevi, only they experience true bliss in the Āgamas.”
[8] “From Pañcavaktra Gaṇeśa were born the Pañcamas: Makhāri, Kālāri, Purāri, Smarāri,”
[9] “and Vedāri. Among these five, whoever instructs is to be regarded as his Guru.”
[10] “The Guru’s gotra should be understood as his gotra in all respects. Marriage within the same gotra should never be performed.”
[11] “If someone does so by mistake, he certainly becomes sinner. Therefore, the gotras of these Pañcamas are distinct.”
[12] “Their pravara, branch, sūtra, varṇa, and mantra are also all different. Likewise, their Guru and āśrama are also separately prescribed.”
[13] “The Pañcama named Makhāri belongs to Vīra-gotra, his branch is Reṇuka-śākhā, and his pravara is Ekakshara.”
[14] “His sūtra is Paḍviḍī, his mulavarna is ‘na’, his kalaśa is green, and his Guru is Revaṇārādhya.”
[15] “His mantra is the ten-syllabled ‘Prasāda’ mantra—‘Om ṛhāṁ ṛhīṁ ṛhūṁ ṛhaiṁ ṛhauṁ namaḥ śivāya’; O Pārvatī, this must be received from the Guru.”
[16] “A householder ( grihastha ) of higher āśrama should wear the iṣṭaliṅga. One possessing these characteristics is called Makhāri Pañcama.”
[17] “From the sūtra of Makhāri Pañcama arose twelve UpaPañcamas; from the Sadyojāta face of Pañcavaktra Gaṇeśa,”
[18] “the leader Makhāri Pañcama was born, and from him these twelve UpaPañcamas arose.”
[19] “O beautiful-faced one, I will tell their names: Śatāṅga, Pramukha, Śarkara, Vṛṣabha,”
[20] “Sahasrākṣa, Sadharma, Viṣama, Mocaka, Vṛkabhēdī, Kuñjarāri, Śeṣa, and Śikhiharita.”
[21] “These twelve UpaPañcamas all originated from Makhāri Pañcama.”
[22] “O beautiful one, the Guru’s gotra should be understood as their gotra also; marriage should be done outside one’s gotra.”
[23] “If one performs marriage within the same gotra, he becomes a sinner. The Pañcama named Kālāri belongs to Nandi-gotra.”
[24] “His branch is Dāruka, his pravara is dwakshar, his sūtra is Vṛṣṭi, and his mulavarna is ‘ma’.”
[25] “His kalaśa is red-colored, and his Guru is Maruḷārādhya. His mantra is the nine-syllabled Māyā-pañcākṣarī,”
[26] “that is, ‘Om ṛhāṁ ṛhīṁ ṛhūṁ ṛhaiṁ namaḥ śivāya’, and this mantra must be received from the Guru.”
[27] “A householder (grihastha) of superior varṇa and āśrama who is always engaged in iṣṭaliṅga worship and possesses these qualities is known as Kālāri Pañcama.”
[28] “From the sūtra of Kālāri Pañcama arose twelve UpaPañcamas; from the Vāmadeva face of Pañcavaktra Gaṇeśa, Kālāri was born.”
[29] “From Kālāri Pañcama arose twelve UpaPañcamas. O lotus-eyed Pārvatī, I will tell their names.”
[30] “Keśarākṣa, Mṛgāri, Nākeśa, Vṛṣa, Śilāṅga, Śṛṅgaśīrṣa, Nīlāmbara, Kuhāsana,”
[31] “Śatabāhu, Bahujihva, Nāgadanta, and Ṣaḍgāvapu—these are the twelve UpaPañcamas.”
[32] “All these originated from Kālāri Pañcama. The Guru’s gotra is to be understood as theirs as well.”
[33] “O Pārvatī, marriage should be conducted outside one’s gotra. O lotus-faced one, marriage within the same gotra should never be done.”
[34] “If someone does so, he becomes a sinner. The Pañcama named Purāri belongs to Vṛṣa-gotra.”
[35] “His branch is Śaṅkukarṇa, his pravara is tryakshara, his sūtra is Muktaguccha, and his mulavarna is ‘śi’.”
[36] “His kalaśa is black/dark blue, his Guru is Rāmācārya ( ekoramaradhya ), and his mantra is the eight-syllabled suksma pañcākṣarī,”
[37] “that is, ‘Om ṛhāṁ ṛhīṁ ṛhūṁ namaḥ śivāya’. Thus is the mantra instruction understood.”
[38] “A householder ( grihastha ) of higher varṇa and āśrama should wear the iṣṭaliṅga, and one possessing these qualities is called Purāri Pañcama.”
[39] “From the sūtra of Purāri Pañcama arose twelve UpaPañcamas; from the Aghora face of Pañcavaktra Gaṇeśa, Purāri was born.”
[40] “From Purāri arose twelve UpaPañcamas. O beautiful one, listen to their names.”
[41] “Agnibhukta, Hārita, Jābāla, Nirjara, Niśita, Śaśāṅka, Lalāṭākṣa, Karākṣaka,”
[42] “Pādāsya, Vikaṭāṅga, Śilāda, and Harinmukha—these are the twelve UpaPañcamas.”
[43] “All these originated from Purāri. The Guru’s gotra is to be understood as theirs.”
[44] “O Pārvatī, marriage should be conducted outside one’s gotra. One who knows śāstra should never marry within the same gotra.”
[45] “If someone does so, he becomes a sinner. The Pañcama named Smarāri belongs to Bhṛṅgi-gotra.”
[४६] Its branch is named Dhenukarṇa, and its pravara is said to be of caturakshara. Its sūtra is called Muktāguccha, and the fundamental letter is “va”.
[४७] Its kalasha is white in color, and its guru is Panditaradhya. Its mantra is the sthula pañcākṣara, consisting of seven syllables,
[४८] namely “Om rhāṁ rhīṁ namaḥ śivāya,” and this is considered the most excellent among all. Having received initiation into such a great mantra,
[४९] a householder ( grihastha ) belonging to the superior varnasrama should always remain engaged in the worship of the iṣṭaliṅga. One who possesses the above-mentioned characteristics should be known as Smarāri Pañcama.
[५०] From the sūtra of that Smarāri Pañcama, twelve upapañcamas arose. From the Tatpuruṣa face of Pañcavaktra Gaṇeśa, Smarāri Gaṇanāyaka was born.
[५१] From that Smarāri Gaṇanāyaka, twelve upapañcamas were produced. O beautiful-faced one, I shall tell you the distinct names of each of them.
[५२] Sahasraśīrṣa, Pītāṅga, Nagamāla, Nirāśana, Yamadyuti, Saptāṅga, Lalitāṅga, Mṛtyunāśana,
[५३] Atanu, Ghoṭavaktra, Nīroga, and Bhava—these are the twelve upapañcamas.
[५४] All these pañcamas have arisen from Smarāri Gaṇanāyaka. O beautiful one, the gotra of the guru should be understood as their gotra as well.
[५५] Leaving one’s own gotra, marriage relations should be made with another gotra; one should never enter into marriage within the same gotra.
[५६] If by mistake someone contracts marriage within the same gotra, he becomes culpable. The Pañcama named Vedāri is said to belong to the Skanda gotra.
[५७] Its branch is named Viśvakārṇa, and its pravara is Pañcākṣara. Its sūtra is Pañcavarṇa, and the fundamental letter is “ya”.
[५८] Its kalasha is yellow-colored, and its guru is Vishvaradhya. Its mantra is the ṣaḍakṣara mahāmantra, which is the root mantra.
[५९] That ṣaḍakṣara mantra is “Om namaḥ śivāya,” and it is considered the greatest among all mantras. Having received initiation into such a great mantra,
[६०] a superior varnasrami householder ( grihastha ) should always wear the iṣṭaliṅga. One who possesses the above-mentioned characteristics should be known as Vedāri Pañcama.
[६१] From its sūtra, twelve upapañcamas arose. From the Īśāna face of Pañcavaktra Gaṇeśa, O Pārvatī, Vedāri Pañcama was born.
[६२] From that Vedāri Pañcama, twelve upapañcamas were produced. O Pārvatī, I shall tell you the distinct names of each of them—listen.
[६३] Paścādṛk, Viśvapuṣṭa, Gomukha, Girivaktraka, Suvarṇa-nakhara, Ajāṅghri, Daśānana, Vipānana,
[६४] Umradeha, Śatapada, Sahasraskandha, and Trimukhaskandha—these are the twelve upapañcamas.
[६५] All these have arisen from Vedāri Gaṇanāyaka. O beautiful one, the gotra of the guru should be understood as their gotra as well.
[६६] Leaving one’s own gotra, marriage should be performed with another gotra; one should never marry within the same gotra.
[६७] If someone mistakenly performs marriage within the same gotra, he become a sinner. One who, abandoning the guru of his own gotra,
[६८] gets the marriage ritual performed by a guru of another gotra becomes a caṇḍāla. Therefore, O Pārvatī, one should perform marriage and other rites only through one’s own guru.
[६९] This alone is praised as the proper path by wise men. One who, even by mistake, performs marriage within the same gotra,
[७०] causes mixing (corruption) of the gotra through union with women of his own gotra. O Pārvatī, in marriage and such rites, there are five types of kalashas of the gurus.
[७१] Sūtra, varṇa, branch, mantra, and pravara—these should all be understood as distinct according to their respective gotras.
[७२] Now I shall explain how the installation of these five kalashas is to be done according to śāstric method. According to respective gotras, there are five types of praṇavas.
[७३] If a person born in the gotra of Makhāri Pañcama (Vīra gotra) is to be married, the learned one should establish the “na”-praṇava of that Makhāri Pañcama at the center.
[७४] Place “ma” in the east, “śi” in the south, “va” in the west, and “ya” in the north.
[७५] If a person born in the gotra of Kālāri Pañcama (Nandi gotra) is to be married, the learned one should establish the “ma”-praṇava at the center.
[७६] Place “śi” in the east, “va” in the south, “ya” in the west, and “na” in the north.
[७७] If a person born in the gotra of Purāri Pañcama (Vṛṣa gotra) is to be married, the learned one should establish the “śi”-praṇava at the center.
[७८] Place “va” in the east, “ya” in the south, “na” in the west, and “ma” in the north.
[७९] If a person born in the gotra of Smarāri Pañcama (Bhṛṅgī gotra) is to be married, the learned one should establish the “va”-praṇava at the center.
[८०] Place “ya” in the east, “na” in the south, “ma” in the west, and “śi” in the north.
[८१] If a person born in the gotra of Vedāri Pañcama (Skanda gotra) is to be married, the learned one should establish the “ya”-praṇava at the center.
[८२] Place “na” in the east, “ma” in the south, “śi” in the west, and “va” in the north.
[८३] The “na” of Makhāri, “ma” of Kālāri, “śi” of Purāri, “va” of Smarāri, and “ya” of Vedāri—these are the praṇavas declared.
[८४] The direction in which a praṇava is placed should be understood as belonging to that respective Pañcama.
[८५] There is no inherent superiority of directions here; the determination is made solely based on the praṇavas.
[८६] Thus, according to śāstric vidhis, the five kalashas should be established, and ten divisions of fruits for naivedya should be prepared; worship should be performed properly with dakṣiṇā and tāmbūla.
[८७] Pārvatī asked, “O Lord Śaṅkara, when only five kalashas are established, why are there ten divisions of naivedya?”
[८८] Īśvara said, “Just as there are five types of Pañcācāryas, there are also five types of Vṛttyācāryas; therefore, ten divisions of fruits are arranged for naivedya.”
[८९] Among those ten parts, five should be full portions and five should be half portions.
[९०] The full portions should be taken by the Mahācāryas in proper according to their praṇava order. If there are any from the upasūtras, their share should also be determined in the same order.
[९१] The half portions should then be taken by the Vṛttyācāryas. One should never take another’s share.
[९२] If someone forcibly takes another’s share, it amounts to equality with superiors (improper comparison), and by unjustly enjoying another’s portion, one attains hell.
[९३] If a Mahācārya takes the share of a Vṛttyācārya, then that share should be given to him; otherwise, it results in loss to him.
[९४] Thus, after performing prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā with the Brahma-mantra, the five kalashas should be installed according to śāstric vidhis.

Thus ends the section on the origin of the Pañcācāryas and the Pañcamas among the Vīraśaiva Brāhmaṇas.
